name: Thread-efficient Partial Rendering
definition: A rendering method that reduces multi-view training overhead by subsampling pixels per viewpoint within a tile and assigning multiple GPU blocks (each with thread count equal to subsampled pixels) to render those specific pixels, eliminating idle threads caused by naive binary masking in tiled rendering.
summary: Thread-efficient partial rendering is a GPU optimization for 3D Gaussian Splatting that maximizes utilization by assigning multiple blocks to a single tile, eliminating idle threads caused by naive binary masking.
